answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with graduated trust tiers: a new identity starts on a small island of capped rewards, like a lone lotus in a pond, and only earns wider access after gathering diverse, independent attestations over time. No single grove of self-created accounts can vouch it upward, because endorsements from clustered or newly made identities count for almost nothing until those endorsers themselves have proven history. Fakes stay quarantined in the low tier, while real agents grow into full participation.
